name: Steven "The Edge" Spector
caption: DPW's own first-ever World Heavyweight Champion, crowned at the fed's Motor City Madness PPV, and still ranked among its top singles wrestlers a year on.

tenures.role: wrestler — DPW World Heavyweight Champion (1 reign)
tenures.source: The fed's own 5/4/96 roster sheet (billed the reigning DPW Heavyweight Champion); its own 23 July 1996 title-lineage sheet ('Steven "The Edge" Spector 7/21/96 to'); and the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter, ranking him #1 (21-8-4) among singles wrestlers behind the three champions.

tenures.note: At An Evening To The Extreme (15 July 1998): came out in the ring to offer himself as "Dreamlover" Trey Porter's partner against the Snake Den, which Porter accepted with a handshake; beat Hakiro Matsuoko in the first round with the Cherry Blossom Bomber and a pin after the Snake Den attacked and Kevin Slater hit Matsuoko with Sweet Dreams, and advanced to face Derek Mota; faced Ronnie D and Simon Lebec in the aisle beside Porter.

name: Hollywood
caption: DPW's own Network Champion, crowned in a 16-man "Rage in the Cage" tournament at Motor City Madness; still a top singles contender and a repeat Network titleholder a year later.

name: "Devastator" Mick Morton
caption: DPW World Heavyweight Champion into 1997, a former first-ever EWA North American Champion, who retained the belt over Hollywood at the interfed New Year's Bash before losing it to Steve Sampson, uncaptured, at Broken Hearts.

tenures.role: wrestler — DPW World Heavyweight Champion (1 reign, in this wing's own record)
tenures.source: The fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter, billing him DPW World Champion (10-1-1); the fed's own New Year's Bash broadcast, retaining the World Title over Hollywood in the DPW/PCW/EWA interfed main event (1 January 1997); a face-to-face interview segment booking his Broken Hearts defense against Steve Sampson, and his own claim there to have been 'the FIRST EWA North American Champion.'

tenures.note: On the fed's cards: lost at Battle Brawl II (30 January 1997) against the other nineteen. Appears in the segments of May Madness: The Anniversary (25 May 1997).

name: "Rising Son" Tony Coltrane
caption: A New York challenger who pushed DPW's undefeated Central Valley Champion the distance at the New Year's Bash before dropping a reversal-filled roll-up finish.

tenures.role: wrestler — DPW Central Valley Championship challenger
tenures.source: The fed's own New Year's Bash broadcast (Central Valley Championship match, lost to Mr. Robinson via roll-up, with ringside interference from Chris Deugau); the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter, ranking him #4 (8-2-1).

name: Daemon "The Dragon" Dempsey
caption: DPW Network Champion by the fed's own late-January 1997 newsletter, who returned in March to call out the man who had since taken his title, The Boogieman.

tenures.source: The fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter, billing him DPW Network Champion (10-4-5); the fed's own 8 March 1997 broadcast, interrupting a Network Title defense to call out The Boogieman on camera.

tenures.note: Billed from Los Angeles, California at 6'8" and 385 pounds, entering to "Hey Man...Nice Shot" by Filter to chants of Dragon; a favorite for the tournament who beat Tommy Marauder the week before. Works a full nelson, a Tiger Driver and a running Liger Bomb. On the card: won at Winter Inferno 97 (15 December 1997) against Chris Deugau; lost at Winter Inferno 97 (15 December 1997) against The Man From Heck. The page pairs Daemon "The Dragon" Dempsey and Tommy Marauder: Dempsey's press conference and a video recap of his win over Marauder, who had beaten him with a sign ("Marauder did take a lot out of me, but the Dragon is still intact.").
